Mount Pisgah
PIZ-guh
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Pisgah; the height (a peak of Mount Nebo) from which Moses viewed the promised land he would not enter.

📖 Biblical Definition

Pisgah was a height in the mountains of Moab, the top of Nebo, from which Moses was given to view the promised land at the end of his life. The LORD had told him he would not cross the Jordan because of his sin at Meribah, but said, "Get thee up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with thine eyes" (Deut 3:27). At the last, "Moses went up... unto the top of Pisgah... And the LORD shewed him all the land" (Deut 34:1), from Gilead to the western sea; "I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither" (Deut 34:4). There Moses died, and the LORD buried him in a valley in Moab, and no man knows his sepulchre. From Pisgah the servant of God saw by faith the inheritance he would not tread in this life. Pisgah stands in the dictionary as the height of seeing-from-afar, a witness to the seriousness of God's discipline even toward His honored servants, and a tender picture of faith that beholds the promised rest from a distance, dying in hope of the better country, content to see and salute the promises afar off though not to enter them in this life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The height (a peak of Nebo) from which Moses, barred for his sin, viewed the promised land before dying (Deut 3:27; 34:1-4); a picture of faith that beholds the inheritance from afar.

MOUNT PISGAH, proper noun. A height in Moab, the top of Mount Nebo.

From which Moses was shown the promised land (Deut 3:27).

He was barred from entering for his sin at Meribah.

"The LORD shewed him all the land" from Gilead to the sea (Deut 34:1).

Where Moses died, and the LORD buried him (Deut 34:5-6).

📖 Key Scripture

Deut 3:27 — "Get thee up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan."

Deut 34:1 — "And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah... And the LORD shewed him all the land..."

Deut 34:4 — "...I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither."

Heb 11:13 — "These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them..."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Pisgah needs no defense from redefinition; its lessons are the seriousness of God's discipline toward His servants and the faith that beholds the promised inheritance from afar.

expand to see more

Discipline-denied correction. Some imagine that great usefulness exempts a servant from the consequences of sin. Moses, the meekest of men and the LORD's faithful servant, was barred from the land for his failure at Meribah, and saw it only from Pisgah. The dictionary holds that God disciplines those He loves and honors, and that even forgiven sin may carry temporal consequence; the height of Pisgah is a sober witness that no rank in God's service places one above His holy government.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is faith that embraces the promises from afar. Moses died on Pisgah in hope, having seen the land he would not tread — a pattern of the saints who "died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off" (Heb 11:13). The dictionary commends this hope: the believer may not enter every promise in this life, but he beholds the better country from the heights of faith, salutes it, and dies content in the God who keeps His word beyond the grave.
